title: Use tote fill thresholds (“Pretty full” vs “Full”) to understand when exchanges occur and why chutes pause
summary: Use the documented tote fullness thresholds—“Pretty full” and “Full”—to interpret expected exchange behavior. The system uses weight and dimensions to assess how full a tote/location is as items sort into it. When a tote reaches “Full,” the system tells Chat that the chute is unavailable so no additional packages come down during the exchange.
when_to_use: When you need to interpret whether an observed exchange/pause behavior is expected based on tote fullness thresholds (“Pretty full” vs “Full”), and specifically whether “chute unavailable” during an exchange explains why packages are not coming down.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as the sole cause analysis when the observed behavior does not match the documented “Full” → “chute unavailable” explanation; escalate for deeper system-side investigation.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Interpret observed exchange behavior using the documented tote fullness threshold logic (“Pretty full” vs “Full”) and the documented “chute unavailable” behavior during exchange.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to observe whether an exchange is occurring and whether the chute is being treated as unavailable (as described: “tells Chat that the chute is unavailable”).

visual_references.description: Training frame containing the documented tote fullness thresholds (“Pretty full”, “Full”) and the behavior: when a tote is full, Chat is told the chute is unavailable so no packages come down during an exchange.

steps.title: Identify the two tote fullness thresholds used by the system: “Pretty full” and “Full.”
steps.purpose: Establish the two documented states that drive exchange-related behavior.
steps.instruction: Use the documented threshold names exactly as stated: “Pretty full” and “Full.”
steps.expected_result: You can clearly distinguish the two threshold labels you will use to interpret observed behavior.
steps.healthy_condition: You are using “Pretty full” for “not full yet, but getting sorted” and “Full” for “no more product can be diverted to this location until an exchange is done.”
steps.failure_condition: You cannot map the observed behavior to either “Pretty full” or “Full,” or you mix up their meanings.

actions.label: Confirm threshold labels
actions.exact_action: Identify the two documented tote fullness thresholds used by the system: “Pretty full” and “Full.”

source_evidence.quote: Two thresholds exist from Chat that an item has accumulated as items sort + Pretty full - Not full, but getting sorted ... + Full - No more product can be diverted to this location until tote. an exchange is done

steps.title: Recall the fullness assessment inputs: weight and dimensions as items sort into the tote/location.
steps.purpose: Ensure your interpretation of “Pretty full” vs “Full” is grounded in the documented assessment method.
steps.instruction: When interpreting tote fullness, use the documented inputs: the software determines how full a location/tote is using weight and dimensions as items sort into the tote.
steps.expected_result: You can explain that tote fullness is determined by software using weight and dimensions (not by chute photo eyes), consistent with the documented logic.
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation ties “Pretty full”/“Full” to software fullness determination based on weight and dimensions.
steps.failure_condition: You attempt to explain “Pretty full”/“Full” using a different mechanism than the documented weight/dimensions-based assessment.

actions.label: Use documented inputs
actions.exact_action: Recall the documented fullness assessment inputs: software determines how full a location/tote is using weight and dimensions as items sort into the tote.

steps.title: Interpret “Pretty full” as approaching exchange consideration (not full yet).
steps.purpose: Provide the correct operational meaning of the first threshold.
steps.instruction: Treat “Pretty full” as “not full yet, but getting sorted,” i.e., the tote is accumulating toward the point where exchange handling begins.
steps.expected_result: You can label the tote state as “Pretty full” when it is not yet at “Full,” and you expect exchange consideration rather than the “chute unavailable” behavior reserved for “Full.”
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation aligns “Pretty full” with “Not full, but getting sorted.”
steps.failure_condition: You treat “Pretty full” as if it already implies “Full” behavior (no more product diverted / chute unavailable).

actions.label: Map to “Pretty full” meaning
actions.exact_action: Interpret “Pretty full” as: not full yet, but getting sorted (i.e., approaching the point where exchange consideration begins).

source_evidence.quote: Pretty full - Not full, but getting sorted

steps.title: Interpret “Full” as no more product diverted until the exchange is done.
steps.purpose: Provide the correct operational meaning of the second threshold that drives chute pause behavior.
steps.instruction: Treat “Full” as “No more product can be diverted to this location until an exchange is done.”
steps.expected_result: You can label the tote state as “Full” and expect exchange gating behavior to prevent additional diversion to that location.
steps.healthy_condition: Your interpretation aligns “Full” with “No more product can be diverted to this location until tote. an exchange is done.”
steps.failure_condition: You treat “Full” as if diversion can continue or as if exchange gating is not expected.

actions.label: Map to “Full” meaning
actions.exact_action: Interpret “Full” as: no more product can be diverted to that location until an exchange is done.

source_evidence.quote: Full - No more product can be diverted to this location until tote. an exchange is done

steps.title: Understand the documented “Full” behavior: Chat is told the chute is unavailable during exchange.
steps.purpose: Connect the “Full” threshold to the operational symptom (chute pause / packages not coming down).
steps.instruction: When a tote is “Full,” use the documented behavior that the system tells Chat the chute is unavailable so that no packages come down while doing an exchange.
steps.expected_result: You can explain why packages stop coming down during an exchange: the chute is treated as unavailable because the tote is full.
steps.healthy_condition: Observed exchange activity coincides with the expected “chute unavailable” behavior described as “tells Chat that the chute is unavailable so that no packages come down while doing an exchange.”
steps.failure_condition: Observed exchange activity occurs but the chute pause behavior does not match the documented “Full” → “chute unavailable” expectation.

actions.label: Map “Full” to chute-unavailable behavior
actions.exact_action: When the system indicates a tote is “Full,” understand the documented behavior: the system tells Chat that the chute is unavailable so that no packages come down while doing an exchange.

source_evidence.quote: When a tote is full, we tell Chat that the chute is unavailable so that no packages come down while doing an exchange

steps.title: Troubleshoot “packages not coming down during an exchange” by checking whether “Full” explains the chute pause.
steps.purpose: Use the threshold-to-behavior mapping to confirm whether the observed symptom is expected.
steps.instruction: If packages are not coming down during an exchange, use the mapping: “Full” implies the chute is unavailable to Chat, which prevents packages from coming down during the exchange.
steps.expected_result: You can determine whether the observed behavior aligns with the documented cause (tote reached “Full” → chute unavailable during exchange).
steps.healthy_condition: Your observed exchange/pause behavior matches the documented “Full” → “chute unavailable” explanation.
steps.failure_condition: Observed behavior does not align with the documented threshold/chute-unavailable explanation.

actions.label: Confirm expected cause
actions.exact_action: If you are troubleshooting why packages are not coming down during an exchange, use the above mapping to confirm whether the “Full” threshold/chute-unavailable behavior is the expected documented cause.

stop_or_escalate_if: If the observed behavior does not align with the documented threshold/chute-unavailable explanation, escalate for deeper system-side investigation beyond this procedure.

source_evidence.quote: When a tote is full, we tell Chat that the chute is unavailable so that no packages come down while doing an exchange

success_criteria: You correctly interpret “Pretty full” vs “Full” using the documented meanings.
You correctly connect “Full” to the documented “Chat told chute is unavailable” behavior during exchange.
When packages are not coming down during an exchange, you can confirm whether this matches the expected “Full” → chute-unavailable explanation.
healthy_conditions: Tote fullness interpretation uses “Pretty full” = not full yet / getting sorted and “Full” = no more product diverted until exchange is done.
During an exchange, the observed chute pause behavior is consistent with “Chat told chute is unavailable so that no packages come down.”
failure_conditions: Observed behavior does not align with the documented “Full” → “chute unavailable” explanation during exchange.
escalation_guidance: If the observed behavior does not align with the documented threshold/chute-unavailable explanation, escalate for deeper system-side investigation beyond this procedure.
